newsitem.title: USA: White House to review tobacco deal for several weeks.
newsitem.headline: White House to review tobacco deal for several weeks.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Friday that the federal government would study an agreement between U.S. states and the tobacco industry for several weeks to see whether it was in the best interests of public health.

"Until now, we have not had the opportunity to review the actual terms of the agreement and we have not concluded whether it is in the best interests of public health," Clinton said in a statement. "Over the next several weeks, we will undertake a thorough public health review."

The White House released the statement in Denver, where Clinton is hosting a summit of the Group of Seven industrialised nations, after state attorneys general announced a landmark settlement with the cigarette industry.

Clinton said he would direct Bruce Reed, his chief domestic policy adviser, and Secretary of Health and Human Services Donna Shalala to consult with public health officials and others and to subject the pact "to the strictest scrutiny."
"They will report to me on whether this agreement represents the best means of protecting the nation's public health interests," he said.

"We must now carefully consider whether approving this proposed settlement will protect the public health -- and particularly our children's health -- to the greatest extent possible," Clinton said. "Protecting the health of the public and these children will be our measure of this proposed agreement."
